pattern_types.name: Conflict avoidance to preserve belonging
pattern_types.definition: When disagreement arises with someone whose approval matters, the person suppresses, delays or dilutes their own position. The driver is fear that conflict will damage the relationship, not lack of opinion.
frameworks: Young's subjugation and approval-seeking schema themes

signs.text: Apologises or hedges before stating a need
Reports agreeing in the moment, then resenting it later
Rehearses conversations to avoid upsetting someone
Describes the other's anger as the worst outcome, above the issue itself
Uses "it's fine" or "not a big deal" about something they then dwell on

signs_against.text: States disagreement directly with close others and reports little distress
Avoids conflict only with people who hold power over them (points to a situational or status driver)

look_alikes.name: Performance-contingent self-worth
look_alikes.tells_apart: Avoids conflict because criticism means failure, not because of fear the relationship will break

look_alikes.name: Control-seeking under uncertainty
look_alikes.tells_apart: Avoids conflict because its outcome is unpredictable; indifferent to closeness

pattern_types.anyone_would: Low-stakes avoidance with strangers or authority only
pattern_types.approved_wording: You seem to protect closeness by keeping disagreements small, even when they matter to you.
pattern_types.prediction_wording: Next time {person} asks for something you'd rather not do, notice whether you say yes before you've decided.

pattern_types.name: Control-seeking under uncertainty
pattern_types.definition: When outcomes are uncertain, the person responds by planning, checking, gathering information or taking over. The discomfort comes from not knowing, and acting on it brings relief even when it changes nothing.
pattern_types.if_situation: An important outcome is unknown or depends on others
pattern_types.then_behaviour: Over-plans, seeks reassurance or takes control
pattern_types.function: To reduce the distress of uncertainty
frameworks: Big Five neuroticism (anxiety facet) with high conscientiousness

signs.text: Re-checks or refreshes for news on something they can't influence
Takes over a shared task rather than waiting on someone
Describes waiting as worse than a known bad outcome
Builds contingency plans for unlikely scenarios
Irritation when plans change at short notice, out of proportion to the cost

signs_against.text: Comfortably leaves an important outcome open for days
Plans heavily only where the stakes are concrete and planning changes the outcome (rational, not distress-driven)

look_alikes.name: Performance-contingent self-worth
look_alikes.tells_apart: Controls to guarantee a good result for self-worth; uncertainty itself is tolerable

look_alikes.name: Conflict avoidance to preserve belonging
look_alikes.tells_apart: Avoids the unknown only when the relationship is at stake

pattern_types.anyone_would: A real crisis where control-seeking is adaptive
pattern_types.approved_wording: Not knowing seems to weigh on you more than a bad answer would, so you reach for control.
pattern_types.prediction_wording: Next time you're waiting on {outcome}, notice how often you check and what changes when you do.

pattern_types.name: Performance-contingent self-worth
pattern_types.definition: The person's sense of worth rises and falls with how well they perform. Falling short is felt as a verdict on the self, not on the work. High standards alone do not qualify; the marker is self-judgement after a miss.
pattern_types.if_situation: Performance is evaluated or falls short
pattern_types.then_behaviour: Self-criticism, over-preparation or avoidance of the task
pattern_types.function: To protect a sense of being worthy
frameworks: Self-critical vs high-standards dimensions of perfectionism (Frost and Hewitt–Flett traditions)

signs.text: Labels self after a mistake ("I'm useless") rather than the act
Discounts success as luck or as the minimum expected
Delays starting or shipping until it is "good enough"
Mood tracks recent output, e.g. a bad workday ruins the evening
Compares own output unfavourably with specific others

signs_against.text: Describes a failure with curiosity and no self-labelling
High standards that bring satisfaction, not dread

look_alikes.name: High standards (healthy)
look_alikes.tells_apart: A miss brings disappointment in the work, not in the self

look_alikes.name: Conflict avoidance to preserve belonging
look_alikes.tells_apart: Fears others' reaction to the relationship, not the verdict on competence

look_alikes.name: Control-seeking under uncertainty
look_alikes.tells_apart: Over-prepares to reduce unknowns, not to prove worth

exclusions.text: Active burnout or job loss in the last month

pattern_types.approved_wording: How well you perform seems to decide how much you allow yourself to feel okay.
pattern_types.prediction_wording: After the next piece of feedback on {domain}, notice whether your first thought is about the work or about you.
